title: Ancient Egypt (KS2)
subject: History
strapline: One of the earliest great civilisations, along the River Nile.
facts: Ancient Egypt was a civilisation that grew up along the River Nile in North Africa thousands of years ago.
The Nile flooded each year, leaving rich soil that let the Egyptians farm in the desert.
Egypt was ruled by kings and queens called pharaohs, who were seen as god-like.
The Egyptians built huge stone pyramids as tombs for their pharaohs.
They preserved dead bodies as mummies because they believed in an afterlife.
They wrote using picture symbols called hieroglyphs.
The Rosetta Stone later helped experts work out how to read hieroglyphs.

quick_quiz.q: Which river was Ancient Egypt built along?
What was an Egyptian king or queen called?
What is the name for the Egyptian picture writing?

teacher_tips: Link the Nile's flood to farming and to why the civilisation thrived there.
Handle artefact replicas and decode simple hieroglyph names.
Place Egypt on a world timeline against British history for perspective.
